notes: Each prompt targets a specific failure mode named in SKILL.md. Prompts are written the way the workshop lead actually talks: a link or a headline plus a casual ask.

evals.name: cross-cutting-chip-controls
evals.prompt: ok so the semiconductor export control story is everywhere today — new rules plus allies grumbling about being squeezed. i've got a background call tomorrow afternoon and want to consult a Brookings expert on it. who should i be talking to?
evals.expected_output: Ranked memo of 3-5 experts spanning at least two of {technology policy, China/Asia, trade enforcement} rather than clustering in one program. Recency verified with dated links. Consult mode read as media comment.

evals.name: recency-trap-absenteeism
evals.prompt: We're pulling together a panel for a convening in the spring on chronic absenteeism and what districts are actually doing about it post-pandemic. Could you find me a Brookings expert or two who'd be good on stage for that?
evals.expected_output: Memo reading the mode as speaking/convening (prominence and range weighted up). Should distinguish scholars with current K-12 work from well-known education names whose recent output is elsewhere, with dated evidence for the distinction.
evals.targets_failure_mode: roster tag mistaken for current activity; fame over fit

evals.name: thin-field-sahel-debt
evals.prompt: I need to brief our program team next week on sovereign debt distress in the Sahel — specifically how the security situation is interacting with restructuring talks. Who at Brookings could help me get smart on this? Memo please.
evals.expected_output: Memo read as decision briefing. Should surface Global Economy and Development / Africa scholars, and — if the field is genuinely thin — say so and flag gaps rather than padding with weak matches.
evals.targets_failure_mode: padding a thin field; failing to report coverage gaps
